chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I heard Ibn Abi Layla say: “In the pre-Islamic era, the blood money was one hundred camels, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله affirmed it. Then he imposed upon the people of cattle two hundred cows, upon the people of sheep one thousand sheep, and upon the people of garments one hundred garments.”

Abd al-Rahman said: So I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام about what Ibn Abi Layla narrated, and he said: “Ali عليه السلام used to say: ‘The blood money is one thousand dinars, and the value of a dinar is ten dirhams. Upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars; upon the people of silver is ten thousand dirhams; ten thousand for the people of the cities; for the people of the deserts, the blood money is one hundred camels; and for the people of the rural lands, two hundred cows or one thousand sheep.’”

key_terms.أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ: one thousand dinars as a standard measure of diyyah
key_terms.أَهْلِ ٱلسَّوَادِ: the people of the cultivated rural lands
key_terms.أَهْلِ ٱلْبَوَادِي: the people of the desert regions
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: ten thousand dirhams as an equivalent legal amount
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: blood money, the prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed amount of diyyah in dinars, dirhams, camels, cows, and sheep in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal amounts of diyyah across different forms of wealth and social settings, such as camels, cattle, sheep, dinars, and dirhams. It preserves an early juridical framework linked to the rulings affirmed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and stated by Amir al-Mu'minin Ali عليه السلام.
